sections.text: Untitled

🍔 外卖配送服务：商家入驻体验优化
饿了么是中国知名的外卖配送平台。通过设计研究，我发现用户在开店前试图处理复杂流程导致流失。我缩短了开店前流程以提高入驻效率，并改进了任务奖励系统帮助商家运营在线店铺、提高存活率。
🤖 AI 商家助手
在这个项目中，我分析了生成式 AI 对饿了么商家在线咨询服务的影响。我设计了合适的交互模型，并从零开始为 App 和 PC 端搭建了对话式助手，旨在提升商家咨询体验并降低人力成本。
🔍 评价分析
"评价分析"对外卖在线店铺运营至关重要，帮助用户了解顾客反馈并改进服务质量。我发现用户很少使用该功能，通过设计研究找到原因并提出创新方案。

sections_en.text: Untitled
Untitled
Untitled
🍔 Food Delivery Service: Restaurant Owner's Onboarding Experience

Eleme (饿了么) is a renowned food delivery service in China, it means “Are you hungry?”
Through the design research, I found that our users tried to deal with the complexity before opening, which led to churn. Our users are also not familiar with online restaurant operations, which leads to a low survival rate. I shortened the pre-opening process to higher onboarding efficiency and improved the task-reward system to help our users operate their online restaurants and increase their survival rate.
🤖 AI Merchant Assistant

In this project, I analyzed the impact of generative AI on Eleme's merchant online consultation service. I designed suitable interaction models and built a conversational assistant for the app and PC from scratch, aiming to enhance merchants' consultation experience and reduce labour costs.
🔍 Review Analysis

"Review analysis" is essential for managing takeout online shops, helping users understand customer feedback to optimize their services and food. However, through research, I found that most users rarely access the review analysis page. This project identifies the reasons through design and user research, and offers innovative design solutions to meet diverse user needs, thereby increasing the number of users using the evaluation analysis feature.

sections.text: 脱口秀是我一生的热爱。把生活的酸甜苦辣变成段子搬上舞台的过程，已经成为我生活中不可分割的一部分。我发现脱口秀和设计之间有很多共通之处：
• 两者都需要对日常生活的敏锐观察力
• 两者都需要不断迭代和打磨素材
• 两者都是把日常痛点转化为有意义的东西——设计将其变为解决方案，喜剧将其变为笑声
• 开放麦本质上就是一种用户测试：你听取观众反馈，迭代，再改进
• 喜剧和设计都需要品味——能注意到大多数人忽略但又能引起共鸣的东西
喜剧不仅提升了我的幽默感，也锻炼了我的演讲和沟通能力。在工作中用讲故事的方式推动想法，更容易获得认同。
从2023年开始，我一直在用英文做脱口秀，学习了 Norah 和 Dave Chappelle 等知名喜剧演员的技巧。我的材料通常围绕文化差异、科技行业的荒诞、以及作为设计师的日常展开。
虽然中国的英文脱口秀场景相对小众，但你可以在上海和北京的各个开放麦活动中看到我的表演。

sections_en.text: Stand-up comedy is a lifelong passion of mine. The process of turning life's highs and lows into jokes and performing them on stage has become an integral part of my life. Comedy and design have many things in common.
• Both require a sharp eye for observing everyday life.
• Both involve constant iteration and refinement of ideas and materials.
• Both turn everyday pain points into something meaningful — design turns them into solutions, comedy turns them into punchlines.
• An open mic is essentially a form of user testing: you listen to audience feedback, iterate, and improve. Sometimes the feedback is so bad that the material never makes it to production 🤣
• Both comedy and design require taste—the ability to notice things that most people overlook but somehow feel off. This sensitivity is a talent shared by great comedians and great designers alike.

Comedy not only enhances my sense of humor but also improves my public speaking and communication skills. It’s a great way to channel negative emotions into something positive, helping me stay optimistic. Bad day? Great-time to write a new joke!
Since 2023, I’ve been doing stand-up in English, learning from well-known comedians like Norah and Davy, popular faces on Rock & Roast.
Although the English stand-up scene in China is relatively niche, you can catch my performances at some international comedy clubs.

sections.text: 在微软工作一年后，我决定重新开始写写AI native designer的转型过程，和AI design workflow的变化，希望能链接更多感兴趣的人。
这次聊的话题是因为前段时间参与了一些Generative UI的项目，因此分享一些总结和反思。看完本文你能获得：

✅ 为什么GenUI重要，明天就可以和同事侃侃而谈
✅ GenUI的形态和行为，设计的重点是什么
✅ 什么Figma不再能设计GenUI，以及我自己的工作流

看完本文你不能获得：
❎ OpenAI的工作机会（但可以增加你获得的概率）
❎ 一只会叫你名字的可爱小猫咪 🐱（但你可以自己vibe coding它）
如何打造一个AI native的GenUI产品呢？其实非常简单👇
正片从这里开始 ～
AI时代，人机界面的体验倒退了
在AI这个时代，我们拥有了足够智能且持续进化的AI系统。讽刺的是，我们的人机交互体验在很多场景反而倒退了——从丰富的图形化界面体验退回到基于文本的对话聊天，能力强大，但表达原始，很多时候信息可读性很低，阅读效率也不高。
AI输出的Text-based界面创造了一种扁平的信息层级，但整段文字的回答非常overwhelming，难以阅读。特别是现在AI也被用在一些任务流的场景中，其实非常低效。用户在大段的文字中寻找相关的信息时，过高的认知负荷和跳跃的重点，会降低用户对AI 的回答的信任感。
GenUI，是AI时代的人机界面
GenUI是由AI实时动态生成的用户界面。
总的来说支持GenUI的AI agent输出的是结构化和可交互的UI，对比当前的大部分Text-based回答：

1. 回答不仅有内容，还有视觉结构和重点
2. 可交互，用户有更高的互动意愿
3. 用户对回答和agent都有更强的信任感
GenUI 的形态
大多数真实世界的AI产品体验可以归为三种界面形态：Chat、Chat+、Chatless。GenUI在不同形态的产品中也有不同的表现。
Chat:
在对话中的交互，对话就是产品。
在这种模式下，GenUI 通常以内嵌形式出现，例如卡片、图表、摘要或工具的结构化区块。比如Open UI提供的开源GenUI能力

Chat+
对话+产品界面共同协作，聊天依然存在，但它只是更大工作区域的一部分。用户通过对话，让AI在可操作的界面中生成GenUI，共同完成任务。比如 Google Stitch在画布种生成UI。

Chatless
界面会在没有任何聊天窗口的情况下自动适配。用户几乎感觉不到“在和 AI 对话”，系统会根据用户的input直接输出新的GenUI更新界面。比如Copilot lab中根据用户的行为自动生成的地图和体验的游戏
GenUI 的形态
有2个影响 GenUI 行为的关键：表达自由度和谁来控制表达

表达自由度（Freedom of Expression）：
决定了系统在视觉和结构上可以让AI “生成到什么程度”。一般来说有3种：

1. 固定组件系统（Low Freedom）：
AI 仅允许调用有限的系统预设组件（比如lists，widget，cards），AI 只能在固定卡片、列表或表单之间选择，不允许结构突破

2. 扩展组件系统（Medium Freedom）：
AI 还是调用有限的系统预设组件，但允许不同组件的拼装，组合，Grouping

3. 开放生成系统（High Freedom）：
AI 可以生成完整的HTML 或free-form布局（比如用design skills让AI自由生成UI）
谁来控制表达（Who Controls the Representation）：
一些场景开发者会定义好应用引用GenUI的规则（比如只能用某 3 种卡片），这种情况下产品规定结构，模型只填数据。
另一些场景会让模型自己决定怎么呈现（如用表格，生成多个卡的Grouping，或输出完整 HTML）。产品不再规定结构，只负责渲染模型输出的内容
大多数现实世界的产品处于中间地带，由应用设定边界，而模型在这些边界内进行自适应。
GenUI 时代，Figma 似乎不再可行
Gen UI的设计成为了一个难题，不像传统的静态UI，GenUI需要测试不同components千变万化的组合。这在Figma中几乎无法完成，因此我们需要打造新的工具，确保上线前就能充分测试GenUI的各种edge cases.
理想的GenUI，和AI可能拼接出的奇怪UI👇
AI Workflow，打造 GenUI 工具
我一直希望让参与设计的 Copilot 能输出内容丰富的UI界面，而不只是text heavy的大段文案。在古法设计时期（1年多前），用Figma手搓很难穷尽所有的组合场景。而现在，只要有Claude code以及产品的Codebase，就可以搭建属于自己的GenUI设计工具。在产品上线之前就能看到自己搭建的GenUI系统在各种场景的表现。
经过调研，我找到一个开源的GenUI库，并理出了实现的技术架构：
• 定义一个GenUI design system
• 和LLM约定好，返回的内容中带有表达GenUI的Tag
• 然后让agent根据规则，将带Tag的返回信息，在浏览器渲染成带有UI的回复内容
我把开源库clone到本地，把库中的GenUI样式调整得尽可能和Copilot相似，然后和Copilot代码库相结合，让我们看看效果！
我询问了一个日本的旅游计划，Copilot 的回答使用了多种GenUI，输出了图文并茂，且可以交互的详细计划👇
对比纯文本的AI回答，GenUI内容结构明显会更有重点，视觉上更有吸引力👇
甚至我输入申请信用卡相关的问题，AI直接生成了我一个可交互的申请流程，可以直接填写提交。
至此，以后要增加新的GenUI 组件和规则，不再需要Figma手搓，只需要向Claude code描述成新的components和规则，甚至让AI自动生成evals（评估系统）测试，就能快速判断新的设计表现是否符合预期。
好啦，虽然还有很多没说完，但是真的要去睡觉了😴 欢迎交流！

sections_en.text: After a year at Microsoft, I decided to start writing again about my transition as an AI-native designer and the evolution of AI design workflows, hoping to connect with more like-minded people.
This time I'm sharing insights from recent Generative UI projects. After reading, you'll gain:

✅ Why GenUI matters — enough to discuss with colleagues tomorrow
✅ GenUI forms and behaviors — what designers should focus on
✅ Why Figma can no longer design GenUI, and my own workflow

What you won't get:
❎ A job at OpenAI (but this might improve your chances)
❎ A cute kitten that calls your name 🐱(but you can vibe-code one yourself)
How to build an AI-native GenUI product? It's actually quite simple 👇
The real content starts here ~
In the AI Era, Human-Computer Interface Experience Has Regressed

In the AI era, we have sufficiently intelligent and continuously evolving AI systems. Ironically, our HCI experience has regressed — from rich graphical interfaces back to text-based chat. Powerful in capability, but primitive in expression, with low readability and poor efficiency.

AI's text-based output creates a flat information hierarchy. Long text responses are overwhelming and hard to read. In task-flow scenarios it's very inefficient. High cognitive load and scattered key points reduce user trust in AI responses.
GenUI: The Human-Computer Interface of the AI Era
GenUI is user interface dynamically generated by AI in real-time.
AI agents supporting GenUI output structured, interactive UI. Compared to current text-based responses:

1. Responses have content WITH visual structure and emphasis
2. Interactive — higher engagement willingness
3. Users have stronger trust in both response and agent
Forms of GenUI
Most real-world AI product experiences fall into three interface forms: Chat, Chat+, and Chatless. GenUI manifests differently in each.
Chat:
Interaction within conversation — the chat IS the product.
In this mode, GenUI appears as embedded blocks — cards, charts, summaries, or structured tool outputs. For example, Open UI's open-source GenUI capabilities.

Chat+
Conversation + product interface working together. Chat still exists, but as part of a larger workspace. Users have AI generate GenUI in an actionable canvas. E.g., Google Stitch generating UI in canvas.

Chatless
The interface adapts automatically without any chat window. Users barely feel they're "talking to AI" — the system outputs new GenUI directly based on user input. E.g., Copilot Lab's auto-generated maps and games.
Forms of GenUI
Two key factors influence GenUI behavior: Freedom of Expression and Who Controls the Representation.

Freedom of Expression:
Determines how far the system allows AI to "generate" visually and structurally. Three levels:

1. Fixed Component System (Low Freedom):
AI can only call limited preset components (lists, widgets, cards). No structural breakthroughs allowed.

2. Extended Component System (Medium Freedom):
AI still calls preset components but allows assembly, combination, and grouping.

3. Open Generation System (High Freedom):
AI can generate complete HTML or free-form layouts (e.g., using design skills for AI to freely generate UI).
Who Controls the Representation:
In some scenarios, developers define GenUI rules (e.g., only 3 card types). The product dictates structure, the model fills data.
In other scenarios, the model decides presentation (tables, card groupings, or full HTML). The product no longer dictates structure, only renders model output.
Most real-world products fall in between — the application sets boundaries, the model adapts within them.
In the GenUI Era, Figma Is No Longer Viable

Designing GenUI is a challenge. Unlike traditional static UI, GenUI requires testing ever-changing component combinations. Nearly impossible in Figma — we need new tools to test edge cases before launch.
Ideal GenUI vs. the weird UI that AI might assemble 👇
AI Workflow: Building GenUI Tools

I've always wanted Copilot to output rich UI, not just text-heavy paragraphs. In the old-school design era (1+ year ago), Figma couldn't cover all scenarios. Now with Claude Code and the product codebase, you can build your own GenUI design tools and preview across scenarios before launch.
After research, I found an open-source GenUI library and mapped out the technical architecture:
• Define a GenUI design system
• Agree with the LLM on a protocol where responses include GenUI tags
• Then have the agent render tagged responses as UI components in the browser based on the rules
I cloned the library locally, adjusted GenUI styles to match Copilot, then combined with the Copilot codebase. Let's see the results!
I asked for a Japan travel plan. Copilot used multiple GenUI components, outputting a detailed interactive plan with rich media 👇
Compared to pure text AI responses, GenUI clearly has better structure, focal points, and visual appeal 👇
I even asked about credit card applications — the AI generated an interactive application flow I could fill out and submit directly.
From now on, adding new GenUI components no longer requires Figma. Just describe new components to Claude Code, even have AI auto-generate evals to validate designs.
Alright, there's still much more to say, but I really need to sleep 😴 Feel free to reach out!

sections.text: 我在构思这个个人网站的时候，我希望网站本身就是一个 AI native 产品，符合我对 AI native 产品的设计原则，我觉得一个AI native 的产品应该符合以下原则：
• 把AI能力从产品中拿走，这个产品就不成立了
• 产品会随着AI模型能力提升而变得更强
• 为Agent设计
在后续迭代中，我还希望我的AI产品：
• Dynamic：行为从简单规则涌现，而不是处处写死规则
• Primitive：从最小单元组合出更大的无限可能
• Constraint: 了解模型能力的边界，在边界内选择最好的设计方案，提供最好的产品体验
我觉得做AI产品和钓鱼很像（对的我也喜欢钓鱼），来得太早或太晚都没有收获（模型能力没达到，或已被模型能力覆盖），而是要判断潮汐趋势，在对的timing下竿。
做AI产品，要提前判断模型能力的发展，让产品能在模型能力的边界处发光。

sections_en.text: When conceiving this personal website, I wanted the site itself to be an AI-native product, aligning with my design principles for AI-native products. I believe an AI-native product should follow these principles:
• Remove AI capabilities from the product, and the product ceases to exist
• The product gets stronger as AI model capabilities improve
• Designing for Agents
In future iterations, I also want my AI product to be:
• Dynamic: Behaviors emerge from simple rules, rather than being hardcoded everywhere
• Primitive: Infinite possibilities composed from the smallest units
• Constraint: Understand the boundaries of model capabilities, choose the best design within those boundaries, and deliver the best product experience

I think building AI products is like fishing (yes, I also love fishing) — arriving too early or too late yields nothing (model capabilities haven't reached the threshold, or have already surpassed it). The key is to anticipate where the boundary will be
Building AI products requires anticipating the development of model capabilities, so the product can shine right at the frontier of what's possible.

sections.text:
这个项目是我还在上学时的一个课程作业，已经过去快10年了，但我还是很喜欢。
因为它提醒我 —— 我是一个builder，不论在有没有AI的时代，把东西做出来，就会让我兴奋！
火焰是最原始的人与光的互动媒介，人们会用双手保护蜡烛的火苗，用嘴吹灭火苗，微微的风也能改变火苗方向。电灯的出现让人与光的交互变得更直接，这个项目尝试用人与火苗的互动方式去重新设计电灯。
我用了不同的sensors，来让这个产品感知周围的温度，光线和大气压力，让后用一块Arduino来根据这些输入控制输出 —— 1个LED灯泡
我希望这个产品是一个有温度的艺术品，而不是科技感满满的电子产品，所以我自己制作硅胶模具，用水泥作为材料，做了好几版不同的产品设计。
这是其中最满意的一个造型，用户可以用火柴点亮它，用手和它互动，以及 —— 像吹生日蜡烛一样熄灭它！
这里有一个来自“古代”的视频展示👇
https://youtu.be/Gt6PV9eqL3g?si=xElQHb_Xjrn926mp

sections_en.text: This project was a school assignment from nearly 10 years ago, but I still love it. Because it reminds me — I'm a builder. Whether or not we're in the AI era, making things come to life excites me!

Fire is the most primitive medium of interaction between humans and light. People cup their hands to protect a candle flame, blow to extinguish it, and even a gentle breeze can change its direction. The invention of electric light made human-light interaction more direct. This project attempts to redesign electric lighting using the interactive language of fire and flame.
I used different sensors to let the product perceive surrounding temperature, light, and atmospheric pressure, then used an Arduino to control the output based on these inputs.

I wanted this product to be a warm piece of art rather than a tech-heavy electronic device. So I made my own silicone molds and used cement as the material, going through several iterations of different forms.
This is my favorite form among them. Users can light it with a match, interact with it by hand, and blow it out like a birthday candle!
